saying: Commenters ask that comparators be anchored to the device's labeled intended user and the care patients would otherwise receive, with acceptance criteria prespecified from the consequence of an incorrect output. Several reject the "median clinician in practice" bar; clinician panels are validated, blinded adjudication instruments with reported inter-rater reliability, and team performance is primary where labeling requires human review.

disagreement.text: Commenters split over benchmarking against actual practice. Some want performance judged against the care available without the device, including delayed or no intervention; others say prevailing or median practice normalizes existing variation and want an evidence-based standard or an absolute safety floor for high-risk functions.

sides.summary: Compare the device to the care patients would actually receive absent it, including no or delayed intervention.
Reject median or prevailing practice as the bar; require an evidence-based clinical standard or absolute safety floor.
